o.text: Inherited from Old Anatolian Turkish یخشی (yaḫşı), which was borrowed from a non-Oghuz subbranch according to L. Johanson, from Proto-Common Turkic *yakšï, derivation of Proto-Turkic *yak- (“to draw near; to fit, to be well-suited”).
Inherited from Old Anatolian Turkish قرداش, قردآش (qardaš). Equivalent to qarın (“womb”) + -daş (“fellow, sharer”). Literally, “those who share the same womb”. Compare Turkish kardeş.
From birlik + -də, the latter being the locative suffix.
